description: Review Standard Operating Procedure — step-by-step procedure for reviewing a VAPT finding. Sourced from problem_definition §11.4 (12-step workflow) and system_responsibility.md.

entries.title: Step 1: Receive the finding
entries.description: Receive a normalized VAPT finding as input. The finding must be a single finding (not a full report). The system processes one finding at a time in v1.
entries.action: Log receipt. Assign trace ID. Proceed to step 2.

entries.title: Step 2: Check data-usage status (governance)
entries.description: Verify the finding's data governance status: usage_approved must be true, usage_scope must be internal or evaluation_only, and redaction must be verified. Governance-failed findings are blocked from review.
entries.action: If governance fails: block review, return human_review with violation reason. If governance passes: proceed to step 3.

entries.title: Step 3: Validate input schema
entries.description: Validate the finding against Input Schema v0.2. Check required fields, data types, enum values, and format patterns. Invalid findings are returned with error details.
entries.action: If invalid: return error result with validation issues. If valid: proceed to step 4.

entries.title: Step 4: Run deterministic rule-based checks
entries.description: Run all 9 taxonomy-based deterministic checks: completeness (COMP), evidence (EVID), classification (CLASS), severity (SEV), CVSS, CWE, impact (IMP), recommendation (REC), and retest (RET). These checks produce review comments and sub-results.
entries.action: Run all checks. Collect comments and sub-results. Proceed to step 5.

entries.title: Step 5: Retrieve relevant EVVO rules (RAG)
entries.description: Query the Knowledge Base for rules relevant to the current review task. Use taxonomy codes, finding domain, and tags as retrieval keys. The retrieved rules provide context for the SLM prompt or additional validation guidance.
entries.action: Retrieve KB entries matching current review context. In v1 rule-based mode: use rules to enhance deterministic checks. With SLM: use rules as RAG context for prompt building.

entries.title: Step 9: Run consistency and evidence checks
entries.description: Run cross-field consistency checks (severity-CVSS alignment, evidence-classification alignment, title-content alignment, recommendation-root-cause alignment). Identify any consistency violations.
entries.action: Run consistency checks. Collect consistency issues. Override classification if evidence-classification rule is violated.

entries.title: Step 10: Determine human escalation
entries.description: Evaluate escalation rules against the review results. Check both automatic triggers (evidence insufficient, severity-confidence mismatch, model disagreement) and conditional thresholds (confidence < 0.7, classification_certainty < 0.6).
entries.action: Evaluate all escalation rules. If any trigger fires: set human_escalation.required = true with reasons and recommended_reviewer. Otherwise: set to false.

entries.title: Step 11-12: Record traceability and return result
entries.description: Assemble the final Output Schema v0.1 result. Record traceability metadata (source document, schema versions, KB version, ruleset version, timestamp). Return the structured review result.
entries.action: Assemble output. Record traceability. Return result matching Output Schema v0.1.
